title: Abridge ambient AI scribe reduced work exhaustion and note time in a stepped-wedge randomized trial at UW Health
summary: In a UW Health randomized trial of 66 practitioners, the Abridge ambient scribe lowered work exhaustion scores by 0.44 points and cut note time by 0.36 hours a day.
account: UW Health, the academic health system of the University of Wisconsin, ran a 24-week stepped-wedge randomized trial of the Abridge ambient AI scribe in ambulatory clinics in Wisconsin and Illinois between 21 August 2024 and 27 March 2025. Sixty-six practitioners were randomly assigned to three six-week sequences for starting the scribe. Of 71,487 notes, 27,092 were drafted with the scribe. Scribe use lowered work exhaustion and interpersonal disengagement on the Stanford Professional Fulfillment Index by 0.44 points on a five-point scale (95% confidence interval 0.25 to 0.62). Time spent on notes fell by 0.36 hours a day. The rise in professional fulfillment did not reach the trial's significance threshold. The drop in work outside work lost significance after the authors removed extreme values. The authors report that note quality scores stayed high and that billing diagnostic codes improved. UW Health bought the licenses under a standard vendor agreement, and Abridge provided no funding.
purpose: Abridge is built to capture clinical conversations and draft visit notes in order to lower documentation burden. Lower exhaustion and less note time are that purpose.
deployer: UW Health (University of Wisconsin Hospitals and Clinics)
location: UW Health ambulatory clinics in Wisconsin and Illinois, United States
